card.title: Short Story 2 — A Respectable Woman (Kate Chopin)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The story at a glance "A Respectable Woman" by Kate Chopin is a short story about a feeling that is never named — which is precisely how such feelings behave. Mrs. Baroda, comfortably married to Gaston, is irritated when her husband's friend Gouvernail comes to stay for weeks on the plantation.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Mrs Baroda's suppressed attraction to Gouvernail — repressed desire vs social respectability.
Her final decision ('I shall treat him better') is ambiguous; discuss what it implies.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: Chopin's restraint: nothing 'happens' outwardly; all the drama is psychological — say this when asked about style.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **Mrs. Baroda** is the story's whole terrain: intelligent, self-aware enough to notice her own unreasonableness, and respectable enough to refuse her own discovery. Her arc is not a fall but a negotiation — feeling observed, resisted, survived, and finally invited back, which is the most honest ending a story of this kind can have.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Desire versus propriety** — the central theme: a respectable woman's capacity for feeling exceeds what her respectability permits, and the story dramatises the negotiation without judging it. **The limits of self-knowledge** — Mrs. Baroda's narration of her own motives is unreliable, and the story trusts the reader to hear what she will not say.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. Why was Mrs. Baroda annoyed by Gouvernail's visit? (2 marks)** A. She had formed a picture of him from rumour — a cynical, tiresome man — and had wanted the summer to herself with Gaston. The annoyance is her stated reason; the story's suggestion is that the dislike was never about who Gouvernail was. **Q. How did Gouvernail actually behave? (2 marks)** A.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Why does Mrs Baroda leave for her aunt's house? (2 marks) — she is troubled by her growing attraction to Gouvernail and fears losing respectability.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "The story never names Mrs. Baroda's feeling, and that is its power." Discuss Chopin's use of restraint. (8 marks)** A model answer treats the omission as the story's central technique: the unnamed impulse on the bench, the unexplained flight to the city, the "overcoming" in the last line — each silence invites the reader to supply what the narrative withholds, and the supplied word…  ·  **‘A Respectable Woman’ — inner conflict (classified)** | Element | Detail | Meaning | |---|---|---| | Mrs Baroda | Respectable wife | Social self | | Gouvernail | Poet, quiet guest | Awakened desire | | Husband Gaston | Oblivious host | Social blindness | | Plantation | Isolated setting | Space for feeling |

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The plot, retold with an eye on its turns The setup is a wife's announcement: she is not going to like Gouvernail — she has heard he is a cynic and had hoped to leave him off the guest list. Gaston laughs; Gouvernail arrives and turns out to be nothing like the rumour: quiet, courteous, tired, asking nothing. Her dislike, deprived of fuel, has nowhere to go.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Third-person limited point of view** — the story's master choice: we live inside Mrs. Baroda's consciousness, which means we know more about her feelings than she admits even to herself — the gap between what she thinks and what she says is the story's space.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Irony in the title: Mrs Baroda's 'respectability' is tested by suppressed attraction to Gouvernail — the gap between appearance and feeling is the story's engine.  ·  Trick 2: Track her internal conflict in three beats: annoyance → fascination → flight to the city → (final hint of surrender) — the beats are the character-answer skeleton.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What does the ending suggest? (2 marks) — her husband's hope that she will 'invite' Gouvernail again hints she has not fully conquered the feeling.
